ScreenR: analysis of pooled shRNA and CRISPR-Cas9 screens

Source: R/ScreenR-package.R
ScreenR-package.Rd

ScreenR finds candidate hits in loss-of-function pooled shRNA and CRISPR-Cas9 screens, comparing a treatment with a control or the time points of a dropout screen. It combines the statistical models of edgeR and limma with the simplicity of the tidyverse, and provides plots for each step of the analysis.

Details

The analysis starts from a barcode count table and an annotation table, which are stored in a ScreenR object (create_screenr_object). The counts are then normalized (normalize_data), checked with quality control plots, and the hits are found with several statistical methods:

  • the Z-score of the barcode log2 fold changes with a gene-level permutation test (find_gene_zscore_hit, Z-score);

  • CAMERA (find_camera_hit);

  • ROAST and FRY (find_roast_hit);

  • a time-course model (find_time_hit) and a test for an effect at every time point (find_consistent_hit).

CRISPR-Cas9 screens can be checked with essential and non-essential reference genes (compute_screen_quality) and corrected for the copy-number bias with CRISPRcleanR (correct_crispr_bias). The results of the methods can be combined with summarise_hits and further filtered with the variance and slope filters (filter_by_variance, filter_by_slope).
